subject: 'Advance imprisonment' by horoscope
alt: Cartoon: a courtroom. On the left, behind a tall wooden bench, a bespectacled judge peers down with a smile. In the middle a stout lawyer in a black coat, a file tucked under his arm, holds up a horoscope chart drawn in red lines and shouts: '...My Lord, according to his horoscope he may make anti-government statements in future, so he should be given a sentence of advance imprisonment.' On the right, in the dock, stands a tired, sad man with an overgrown beard and a white kurta. The cartoonist's signature is at the bottom left.
chutki: A horoscope in place of evidence, and in place of a crime, a statement not yet made. The lawyer waves a sheet of red lines and says the stars show this man may one day speak against the government, so he should be jailed in advance. Up above, the judge smiles, and the man in the dock, his beard grown long, listens in silence, as if he has heard this argument many times before.

Dhodapkar's jab is at a practice in which years of imprisonment without trial no longer seem the exception. Everyone has heard of anticipatory bail; the cartoon coins its opposite: advance imprisonment. When someone is held for what he might do, what need is there for evidence, witnesses or argument? A horoscope will do.
